expectations.text: Correctly applies the CS-coefficient thresholds (0.25 minimum, 0.5 acceptable)
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states: 'The field thresholds (Epskamp, Borsboom & Fried, 2018) give three zones: ≥0.50 = acceptable, ≥0.25 = minimum to interpret, <0.25 = do not interpret.' Both thresholds are correctly stated and applied to all four indices.

expectations.text: Concludes that Closeness and Betweenness should not be interpreted given the CS values
expectations.evidence: The table marks both as 'Do not report or interpret,' the text says 'Drop Closeness and Betweenness entirely,' and the suggested write-up states 'Closeness (CS = 0.13) and betweenness (CS = 0.05) fell below the minimum interpretable threshold of 0.25 and are not reported.'

expectations.text: Concludes that Strength and Expected Influence are interpretable but with caution
expectations.evidence: Both are placed in the 'interpretable but fragile' zone with the directive to 'Interpret with explicit hedging.' The write-up template says 'these findings should be interpreted with caution and treated as hypothesis-generating.'

expectations.text: Recommends focusing on edge ordering rather than absolute edge values when CIs are wide
expectations.evidence: 'Absolute weight values are not interpretable. Don't say the edge between nodes A and B was strong (weight = 0.42).' The response also elevates the structural presence/absence of edges as more trustworthy than weight magnitude, clearly directing away from interpreting raw weight values.

expectations.text: Recommends the bootstrapped difference test before making specific edge or node comparisons
expectations.evidence: 'Run the bootstrapped difference tests and only highlight contrasts where the CIs on the difference don't cross zero' and 'use the difference test output (differenceTest() in bootnet) to identify which edge pairs are distinguishable.' Same logic applied to node centrality comparisons.
